main.title: World of Goo
main.summary: World of Goo is a physics-based puzzle video game developed and published by independent game developer 2D Boy.

cards.heading: Building a route from the creatures themselves
cards.text: World of Goo is a physics-based puzzle video game developed and published by independent game developer 2D Boy. The game was released on Windows and Wii  on October 13, 2008, with releases on Nintendo Switch, OS X, Linux, and various mobile devices in subsequent years. World of Goo has the player use small balls of goo to create bridges and similar structures over chasms and obstacles to help other goo balls reach a goal point, with the challenge to use as few goo balls as possible to build this structure.

cards.heading: An independent game finds commercial success
cards.text: The game was nominated for numerous awards—the Seumas McNally Grand Prize, Design Innovation Award, and Technical Excellence—at the Independent Games Festival, and has gone on to win several other gaming awards, such as Outstanding Achievement in Game Design at the 12th Annual Interactive Achievement Awards. The game was critically acclaimed and became one of the earliest examples of a commercially successful indie game.

cards.heading: A return with World of Goo 2
cards.text: A sequel, World of Goo 2, was released on August 2, 2024, in collaboration with Tomorrow Corporation.

main.title: Advance Wars: Days of Ruin
main.subtitle: Strategy after the catastrophe
main.summary: Advance Wars: Days of Ruin is Intelligent Systems' Nintendo DS strategy game set after a meteor disaster has devastated civilisation. Known as Dark Conflict in Europe, it follows survivors trying to organise protection and rebuild amid competing military forces. The familiar turn-based contest of infantry, vehicles, aircraft and ships remains, but the new cast and damaged world change its tone. A position on the map is now presented as a resource for people struggling to survive, giving the series' territorial decisions a more severe narrative setting.

cards.heading: Strategy after the catastrophe
cards.text: Advance Wars: Days of Ruin is Intelligent Systems' Nintendo DS strategy game set after a meteor disaster has devastated civilisation. Known as Dark Conflict in Europe, it follows survivors trying to organise protection and rebuild amid competing military forces. The familiar turn-based contest of infantry, vehicles, aircraft and ships remains, but the new cast and damaged world change its tone. A position on the map is now presented as a resource for people struggling to survive, giving the series' territorial decisions a more severe narrative setting.

cards.heading: Put the commander in the field
cards.text: Commanding officers can join a chosen unit, creating an area around it in which nearby forces receive benefits. Their influence is therefore tied to a visible position on the battlefield. Moving that unit forward can support an attack while also exposing an important part of the army. Unit experience adds another reason to preserve a successful force. These changes bring strategic advantages down onto the map, where the player can see which units are protected, which are isolated and what a retreat would give up.

cards.heading: Build a way out of the ruins
cards.text: Factories and captured properties sustain the familiar cycle of income, production and advance. Terrain and unit matchups determine where that investment can be used safely, while new units and changed rules require fresh judgement from returning players. Multiplayer and custom maps extend the system beyond the campaign's ruined world. Days of Ruin shows how recognisable pieces can support a different atmosphere: the clear grid still makes a complicated battle readable, but the story surrounding each contested settlement gives its capture another kind of weight.

main.title: Burnout Paradise
main.summary: Burnout Paradise is a 2008 racing video game developed by Criterion Games and published by Electronic Arts for PlayStation 3, Xbox 360 and Microsoft Windows.

cards.text: Criterion Games released Burnout Paradise in 2008, taking the racing series into the open streets of Paradise City. Electronic Arts published the original PlayStation 3 and Xbox 360 editions, with a Windows version following. It was the first Burnout released for Windows.

Paradise's gameplay is set in the fictional "Paradise City", an open world in which players can compete in several types of races. Players can also compete online, which includes additional game modes, such as "Cops and Robbers". Several free game updates introduce new features such as a time-of-day cycle and motorcycles. The game also features paid downloadable content in the form of new cars and the fictional "Big Surf Island".

The game received overwhelmingly positive reviews upon release, with aggregate score sites GameRankings reporting an average score of 88% and Metacritic reporting an average score of 88 out of 100. The game won several awards in 2008, with Spike TV, GameTrailers and GameSpot all awarding it Best Driving Game. Reviewers felt the game had an excellent sense of speed, and praised the open world gameplay, a first for the Burnout series. Burnout Paradise is considered by some to be one of the greatest video games ever made.

A remastered version, titled Burnout Paradise Remastered, which includes all downloadable content (except the Time Savers Pack) and support for higher-resolution displays, was released on 16 March 2018 for PlayStation 4 and Xbox One, and on 21 August for Windows. The online service for the original version of the game was permanently discontinued in August 2019. The remastered version for Nintendo Switch with refreshed online servers was released on 19 June 2020.

main.title: Super Smash Bros. Brawl
main.subtitle: A meeting that becomes an adventure
main.summary: Super Smash Bros. Brawl is Nintendo's 2008 fighting game for Wii, directed by Masahiro Sakurai. Up to four players bring characters from different series into the same arena, including newcomers Snake and Sonic. Alongside those matches, The Subspace Emissary gives the cast a shared adventure through side-scrolling stages.

cards.heading: A shared arena
cards.text: Super Smash Bros. Brawl is Nintendo's 2008 fighting game for Wii, directed by Masahiro Sakurai. Up to four players bring characters from different series into the same arena, including newcomers Snake and Sonic. Alongside those matches, The Subspace Emissary gives the cast a shared adventure through side-scrolling stages.

cards.heading: Fighting for a way back
cards.text: Every hit raises a fighter's damage percentage, making later blows send them farther. A player near the edge has to judge whether to attack again or leave enough room to recover. Jumps and special moves can bring a launched character back towards the platform, where another fighter may be waiting to intercept them. The Smash Ball adds a new contest within the match: breaking it grants a character-specific Final Smash. Chasing it can offer a decisive advantage while drawing everyone towards the same dangerous part of the stage.

cards.heading: A journey between worlds
cards.text: The Subspace Emissary takes familiar fighters through enemy-filled routes, linking their journeys with short animated scenes. Movement and attacks carry over from the arena, but a platform or a group of enemies gives them another purpose. The adventure makes room for encounters between characters whose original games have very different worlds. Seeing them help one another gives the crossover a story as well as a roster, with the next stage continuing a journey that a regular match would have ended.

cards.heading: Making room for another match
cards.text: Stage Builder lets players arrange their own terrain, choose its scale and background, then test how a fight moves through it. A platform placed slightly higher can change a landing or leave an awkward gap, so trying the design becomes part of making it. Music offers another way to shape a familiar space. My Music adjusts how often each available track plays on a stage, while collected CDs expand the selection. A favourite arena can gradually acquire a soundtrack chosen around the games its players remember.

main.title: Devil May Cry 4
main.summary: Devil May Cry 4 is a 2008 action-adventure game developed and published by Capcom.

cards.heading: Nero and Dante
cards.text: Devil May Cry 4 is a 2008 action-adventure game developed and published by Capcom. It was released for the PlayStation 3, Xbox 360, and Microsoft Windows platforms. It is the fourth installment in the Devil May Cry series and is written by Bingo Morihashi and directed by Hideaki Itsuno. The story follows Nero, a young man possessing demonic powers who is on a mission to stop the series' main character, Dante, after he assassinates the leader of the Order of the Sword. The player assumes the role of both Nero and Dante as they fight enemies using their demonic powers and a variety of weapons.

cards.heading: Developing for several platforms
cards.text: Devil May Cry 4 is the first entry in the series to be released simultaneously for multiple consoles. During its development, Capcom focused on each version achieving the same visual quality using the MT Framework game engine. Around eighty people formed the team that created the game. Nero was introduced to attract the new gamers. Dante's popularity with gamers proved challenging because the developers needed to use him as a supporting character in the story.

cards.heading: Reception and sales
cards.text: Critical reception to Devil May Cry 4 was positive. It was praised for its challenging difficulty, its visuals and Nero's characterization as a new protagonist. However, it was criticized for its backtracking in Dante's stages and a troublesome camera. The game sold over three million units worldwide, becoming the series' best-selling title before the release of its sequel. Bingo Morihashi adapted it into a two-volume light novel.

cards.heading: Special Edition expands the cast
cards.text: It was released on iOS as Devil May Cry 4: Refrain in February 2011. A remastered version of the game was released in June 2015 as Devil May Cry 4: Special Edition which adds the option to switch between English and Japanese voice tracks in the Japanese release, improved visual effects and textures, in-game re-balancing, additional costumes, and three bonus playable characters: Vergil, Lady and Trish. A sequel, Devil May Cry 5, was released on March 8, 2019.

main.title: Etrian Odyssey II: Heroes of Lagaard
main.subtitle: A castle above the labyrinth
main.summary: Etrian Odyssey II: Heroes of Lagaard is Atlus and Lancarse's Nintendo DS dungeon role-playing game about an adventuring guild climbing toward a floating castle. The Grand Duchy of High Lagaard recruits explorers to investigate the forested Yggdrasil Labyrinth and the treasure said to lie beyond it. The player creates a party, equips it in town and enters the maze a step at a time. The destination gives the expedition a clear upward direction, while every new floor adds another place that must be understood before the next climb.

cards.heading: A castle above the labyrinth
cards.text: Etrian Odyssey II: Heroes of Lagaard is Atlus and Lancarse's Nintendo DS dungeon role-playing game about an adventuring guild climbing toward a floating castle. The Grand Duchy of High Lagaard recruits explorers to investigate the forested Yggdrasil Labyrinth and the treasure said to lie beyond it. The player creates a party, equips it in town and enters the maze a step at a time. The destination gives the expedition a clear upward direction, while every new floor adds another place that must be understood before the next climb.

cards.heading: Draw a dependable return journey
cards.text: The lower screen carries a map drawn with the stylus while the first-person view shows the passage ahead. More annotation symbols allow a more detailed record than in the first game. Warp points can shorten the journey home, making their positions valuable information when the party needs rest or supplies. A map earns its usefulness through repeated visits. The player who records a turning carefully during a healthy expedition may rely on that same mark later, when the party is deciding how much danger lies between it and safety.

cards.heading: Every step also moves a threat
cards.text: Ordinary encounters interrupt travel, while visible FOEs move around the labyrinth according to their own patterns. Since time advances with actions, observing a route can make it possible to pass a dangerous creature without fighting. New classes, including Gunner, War Magus and Beast, expand the choices available when building a guild. The sequel develops the original expedition rather than abandoning it: another set of specialists and clearer maps can support a better plan, but the player still has to decide when a promising journey should end with a retreat to town.
